first cpix implementation

Versioned PIFF track encryption boxes report the default IV length after the fixed KID. Only a legal IV size (at most 16 bytes) is included, matching the CPIX key-record layout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reject invalid CENC IV metadata before decryption

Validate key records and IV sizes before configuring the decrypter. Check multikey SAI indices against the current declared key count so key-info changes cannot expose undeclared trailing records.

Keep the shared validator available without ISO media support and add regression coverage for valid and malformed IV metadata.

PIFF boxes with subsample flags set report that same legal IV length in the default key info.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix PIFF default key-info size

The PIFF default-info getter reports 19 bytes for a 20-byte key
record. This truncates the advertised KID and causes CENC validation
to reject valid PIFF streams.

Return the key-info array's size. AES-CBC PIFF (AlgorithmID 2) also
reports one legal default IV length after that record. Add a regression
test that creates PIFF protection through the public API and checks the
returned size, record contents, and validation.

Verify valid PIFF playback, unchanged PIFF+CENC decryption output,
and all 13 existing CLI reproduction cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: gf_isom_cenc_get_default_info_internal advertises the PIFF default key-info length, and the unchanged walker gf_cenc_key_info_get_iv_size consumes that length. The walker starts at key_info[3] and steps by 17. With key index 0 it never returns on the first record; after a non-zero IV it lands on index 20 (struct padding inside the 88-byte PIFF box, which is zero), then on index 37. It reads key_info[37] only when the advertised size is at least 37. That index is 13 bytes past the 88-byte allocation (key_info begins at offset 64). Each edited commit adds at most one legal IV length, key_info[3] when it is 1..16, and each checks that bound only against the base record, not the running total. The cpix commit adds it for a non-zero box version while the base length is still 19 (19+16=35). The IV-metadata commit adds the same length for non-zero subsample flags, again from base 19. The size fix replaces 19 with sizeof(key_info) (20) and adds the same length for AlgorithmID 2. One addition yields 35 or 36, so the walker stops before index 37. Any two additions yield at least 51, so the walker reads key_info[37]. Deleting any one of the three diffs leaves the other two additions, and the overflow remains. Normal PIFF (version 0, flags 0, AlgorithmID 1) takes none of the additions and still reports 20 bytes.
